note: Candidate-set miss. The five slots concentrated on likely starting attackers and omitted a lower-frequency midfield scorer. Exact scorer markets remain highly diffuse; recent scoring and expected lineups should inform the set, but one slot should remain for a credible midfielder or substitute rather than over-covering similar forwards.

Covered outcome at 12%, though not top-ranked. Including a geographically and operationally diverse set prevented a total miss, but the forecast overweighted Balikatan without sufficiently matching the casualty wording and participating service branches to the exercise.

Strong top-outcome hit. Mercedes had won all three opening races, Kimi Antonelli had the relevant pole signal, and the 73% forecast appropriately retained uncertainty for extensive rival upgrades and sprint-weekend volatility.

Top-outcome hit after updating to the two confirmed finalists. Peshawar's stronger league campaign, rest advantage and Babar Azam's form justified the edge, while Hyderabad's seven wins in eight games kept the forecast calibrated rather than overconfident.

Candidate-set miss. The forecast leaned toward hacktivist and ransomware brands but omitted ShinyHunters, a prominent data-theft and extortion group well matched to a platform breach. Cyber-attribution sets should distinguish disruption, ransomware and credential/data-theft actors before selecting names.

Correct person but likely strict-format miss. The accepted format required the full official name, and omitting Delgado exposed the forecast to exact-string failure despite strong substantive identification. For named officials, copy the complete official English name from the source or institutional record.

Candidate-set miss. The forecast treated the pledge as most likely to draw criticism from the largest parties and omitted the Green Party, whose civil-liberties and migrant-rights positioning was structurally well matched. Party-reaction markets need the full set of ideologically salient critics, not just the largest parliamentary competitors.

Severe overconfidence and branding miss. Reporting on the internal Maritime Freedom Construct did not establish the future public launch name; the official label was Project Freedom. Internal programme descriptions and public-facing initiative names should be treated as separate uncertain variables, with substantial mass reserved for plausible rebranding.
